design_rationale:
WHY THIS MAKES A GOOD TEST. The caller asks for one everyday thing — more included miles on a long rental, charged to the card the trip runs on — and says nothing else of substance. Everything that decides the two scored numbers has to be read out of the marketplace's rules and reconstructed from the reservation's own records: how many miles a top-up must cover, which measure of "the rest of the trip" applies, which block the miles are sold in, what room is left under the reservation's included-mile ceiling, what a block costs for a trip billed under a corporate protection election, and how the line is metered. The difficulty is not in choosing a tool: there are two writes and the policy names each of them once. It is in (a) noticing that the unused-mile figure standing on the reservation is stale and that the mileage record has to be reconciled instead, (b) reading the six rules that move the granted figure off the 1250 miles the standard reading gives, (c) discovering from the pricing rule itself that the price cannot be fixed until the miles stand on the record, so the grant has to be written first, and (d) getting both numbers exactly right. An agent that reads only the two computation documents computes 1250 miles and 1166.00 dollars, confidently and wrongly.

SCOPE. Already occupied before this task: nothing; this is task 0 of the difficulty. This task claims the policies trips_ext_mileage_topup_grant and trips_ext_mileage_topup_pricing and the tools grant_mileage_topup_0373887d (owner agent) and pay_for_mileage_topup_d571ad94 (owner user). It therefore claims the mid-trip mileage top-up space: the granting of bought included miles (subject trips_mileage_allowance_granted) and the pricing of that purchase (subject trips_reservation_charge_posted, charge_basis extra_miles_package). Left for task 1: everything about surcharges on the reserved period itself, extension quoting on the extension request register, cancellations, fuel settlement, late returns and refunds. Task 1 takes the young-driver surcharge line (a different charge basis on the same subject event, its own tool) and the extension quote on the extension register; neither reads or writes anything this task claims, and no policy, tool or route has been reserved beyond the two claimed here.

THE STEP 0 DRAW, AS PRINTED. `.venv/bin/python skills/erl-task-instantiate/scripts/draw_counts.py env/env_0015_car_sharing_marketplace/tasks/trip_booking_and_settlement_desk --tasks 2` printed for this task: {"task": 0, "key": "env_0015_car_sharing_marketplace/trip_booking_and_settlement_desk/0", "prerequisite_problems": 1, "problems": 2, "factor_counts": [6, 5]}. The tree therefore carries exactly one prerequisite problem besides the root, and the two computations carry 6 and 5 declared factors. trips_ext_mileage_topup_grant took the 6; trips_ext_mileage_topup_pricing took the 5.

PROBLEM-TREE CARD. Root problem: trips_ext_mileage_topup_pricing — what the customer's request points at is the purchase going onto her card. Prerequisite problem: trips_ext_mileage_topup_grant. One edge, from the pricing policy to the grant policy.
  kind: value_input. gate: the compute binding granted_miles of the pricing policy.
  form: state. The prerequisite sentence, carried verbatim in the pricing policy's own rule, is "The price of a mileage top-up is fixed only after the miles it adds stand on the reservation's included-mile record."
  Four-point test: (1) it joins this policy's own result ("the price of a mileage top-up") to what it waits on with the ordering connective "only after"; (2) its far side is a record-visible state — miles standing on the reservation's included-mile record, which is what the trip usage lookup shows — and names no action, no performer and no tool; (3) it carries no tool name, no policy id and no snake_case or hex token; (4) it is written at exactly the strength of the edge: a hard requirement ("only after"), scoped to the miles this top-up adds and to nothing wider. The affirmative direction is the one this desk would use, because a charge is fixed only after the thing it is charged for stands on the record.
  Exactly one write of this difficulty brings that state about: the grant of a purchased top-up of included miles, which is what trips_ext_mileage_topup_grant's rule provides for; no other policy in this charter books miles onto a reservation's allowance. Derivation: the sentence says the price waits on miles standing on the record as added by this top-up; the trip usage lookup shows the record carries only the plan allowance granted at confirmation and three odometer readings; the grant policy's rule states how many miles a bought top-up adds and that they are granted to the reservation. One action follows, and it is the one recorded as resolved_by.
  Why it does not hold at the opening: initial_state.trips_usage carries exactly one grant row on this reservation, 7cec7ea6-38d8-4bd4-80ae-7a9abaaf0b6b with grant_reason "plan_allowance", and three rows of event_type trips_mileage_usage_recorded; no row carries grant_reason "purchased_package", so the miles a purchase could be priced for come to nothing.
  Topological order: trips_ext_mileage_topup_grant, then trips_ext_mileage_topup_pricing. There are no parallel edges, so nothing can be reordered.
  Per-edge deletion sensitivity (Step 5 run): replaying the call with the grant write skipped leaves the pricing policy's granted_miles at 0.0, its line price at 0.00 and the scored purchase_amount at 0.00 against 814.40, and the terminal records lack the 3600-mile grant row entirely.
  user_scenario mentions no prerequisite: see prerequisite_closure.no_user_hint. The tool layer validates nothing: see prerequisite_closure.tools_do_not_block.

BASE-INVARIANT CARD.
  Write 1, subject trips_mileage_allowance_granted. Governing base policy: trips_evt_mileage_allowance (the only base policy whose subject carries that event). Its eligibility allowance_window_open applies: "Allowance records are written only while the reservation is in the booked, in_progress or completed state, so that no allowance can be moved on a reservation that has been cancelled or closed for billing." Authority: system record, pre-action, correlated on trips_bookings.booking_id, which is the tool's booking_id argument. At frozen_time the reservation's status is in_progress, so the gate holds; had the call been about the settled weekend reservation the gate would fail and no top-up could be granted at all. This policy supersedes three clauses of that base policy, each declared in its overwrite and each naming the base words it replaces. First, "A guest may buy further miles in whole packages only" is replaced by "A top-up of included miles is granted in whole blocks, the standard block being five hundred miles", so the quantum a purchase comes in is the block and not the plan's package. Second, "a package bought mid-trip is granted in full and charged in full even where fewer miles are eventually driven" is replaced by the sentence that sizes a top-up from the daily included-mile measure, the days still to run, the miles still unused and the reserve, so how many miles a mid-trip purchase adds is this policy's question and not base's. Third, and this is the clause the base sentence uses to forbid exactly the exception this policy makes, "capped at the plan's per-booking ceiling however long the reservation runs" is replaced by the sentence that holds the grant down to the room left under an included-mile ceiling of five thousand miles as standard, eight thousand on a long reservation with no overage charged and six thousand on a long reservation that has been charged one. Nothing else of that base policy is touched, and the rest of it stays in force and is inherited: miles are granted to the reservation and not to the guest, the grant made when a reservation is confirmed is still the plan's daily allowance over the reserved days, an extension's miles are granted as their own record, a telematics reading is authoritative where one exists, and readings consume the allowance in the order they are taken. The base per-booking ceiling and the extended one therefore never both speak: the extended figure is in force here because the overwrite names the base clause it retires. No time gate governs this write.
  Write 2, subject trips_reservation_charge_posted. Governing base policies: trips_evt_reservation_pricing and trips_evt_payment_recovery. The pricing policy's eligibility booking_open_for_pricing applies: "a line is posted only while the reservation is in the requested, booked or in_progress state". At frozen_time the reservation is in_progress, so it holds; on the settled weekend reservation it would fail. Its other clauses stay in force and are inherited unchanged: the locked daily rate is the basis of every later line, every line carries the basis it was priced on so that two lines posted on the same day stay separable, and a line not raised is not a line raised at zero — which is why the mileage purchase goes on as its own line with charge_basis extra_miles_package. trips_evt_payment_recovery carries no structured eligibility for this write; its scope is how a declined charge is re-presented and what an unpaid balance stops, and it is recorded as policy_scope. The price of extra miles, however, is a quantity base publishes elsewhere - on trips_evt_mileage_allowance, whose package sentence carries the plan's package price and package size - so that policy is named in this one's base_policy_refs and its package sentence is declared superseded in the overwrite, replaced by the standard line price of this policy: the block price, less the volume concession, charged for each priced block of five hundred miles the top-up added. Without that declaration base's published package price and this policy's block price would both stand, and the same purchase would have two prices. No time gate governs this write either, so temporal_feasibility is empty.

BUSINESS-OBJECT CARD. The narrowest object is the guest's live reservation 9c741700-7c1a-44fc-b463-4db182e7e04c, priced under the Keyturn Monthly Rate Plan, in progress from 2026-08-05 to 2026-10-09. Correlation key: booking_id, carried on every charge line, every usage record and the protection election. Rows that enter the aggregates: the four usage rows on that booking (the 3750-mile plan grant and the three odometer readings of -1150, -1100 and -550) and, for the overage test, the charge lines on that booking. Rows excluded by the same key: everything on the settled weekend reservation dd2889df-3d5d-4f5d-a813-a2ad339c252f — its 750-mile grant, its -835-mile return reading, its base rate, trip fee and, above all, its 28.00 mileage overage line, which is the near-miss of the granting computation: folded in it drops the included-mile ceiling from 8000 to 6000 and the granted miles from 3600 to 2250, recomputed. The pricing computation has its own, on the other side of the charter: the daily protection fees charged on this trip's election stand as two rows, 1984.00 raised for the first thirty-one days and 704.00 for the next eleven, and the corporate block price is reached only by totalling both. A reader who takes the later row alone reads 704.00, and a reader who takes the earlier one alone reads 1984.00; either falls short of the two-thousand-dollar corporate threshold, the block price reverts to the standard 145.00 and the price becomes 958.40 instead of 814.40, recomputed. The fuel reading on the live reservation is excluded by the rule's filter on odometer readings and books no miles, so folding it in changes nothing and it is not claimed as a near-miss. Nothing on this reservation has been settled, reversed or compensated, so no existing line offsets any other.

WORLD, ROW BY ROW, AND WHAT EACH CARRIES. The customer row carries the identity the caller states and the driver score of 82 that keeps the Monthly plan's deposit line legitimate (its waiver score is 85). The live booking carries the rate plan, the in_progress status both gates read, the reserved hours of 1584.0 that make the reserved period 66 days, the dates every span is measured from, the included miles total of 3750 and the stale unused-mile figure of 1500. The stale figure is the deliberate cache: it was carried forward after the second reading (3750 - 1150 - 1100 = 1500) and has not caught the third reading of -550, so the record leaves 950. Remove it and the first factor stops biting. The weekend booking and its five rows exist to carry the excluded overage line and to make the guest a real member with a history. The three odometer readings carry the dates, the sources and the deltas that decide four of the six granting factors and the handling charge on the pricing side; the host-reported latest reading is what makes the handling charge 12.00 rather than nothing. The protection election on the live trip, written as Keyturn Business Traveler Protection and active, together with its two daily protection fee lines of 1984.00 and 704.00, is the cross-difficulty evidence the block price rests on. Those two figures are what the guestplan charter produces for that level and no other: Keyturn Business Traveler Protection charges a daily flat protection fee of 64.00 billed daily in arrears, so thirty-one days of cover from 2026-08-05 come to 1984.00 and the eleven days to 2026-09-15 come to 704.00, the election's coverage_days of 42 is the days charged for, and its protection_fee_balance_due of 2688.00 is the sum of the two lines. That level charges nothing for a declared additional driver, which is why the one declared driver on this election carries no fee line. The declined election on the weekend trip is a second near-miss, excluded because the block-price rule reads the election attached to this trip; it carries no protection fee lines at all, which is what Keyturn Declined Protection charges. No automatic clause of the base charter is lit by any of these rows: no mileage settlement is due while the trip is in progress, no fuel settlement is due before the return, no late return has occurred, nothing is unpaid past its retries, and the weekend trip is settled and closed. A standing constraint on any reseed of this world: the miles the ledger sums are every mile the reservation's readings have booked, so no two readings may cover the same handover. Base settles that case by making a telematics reading authoritative over a host or guest one, and the sum here takes the readings as booked rather than choosing between them; the three readings on this reservation are dated 2026-08-19, 2026-09-04 and 2026-09-16 and no two cover one handover, so the two readings agree and nothing is overridden.

PERSONA. Renata is brisk and slightly harried, calling from a car park mid-errand, and the text is written as narration about her rather than as a script: what she volunteers, what she will only say if asked, and what she does when the agent says something. She volunteers the goal and her name and mobile, because that is how she starts calls; she gives date of birth, ZIP, licence number and email only when the agent needs more; she answers trip questions from what she can actually see and remember. Her one piece of pushback is natural and carries no policy: the app told her about 1500 included miles were left, she does not believe it after the driving she has done, and she asks for it to be checked. She does not say which figure should be used instead, and the ladder that decides it turns on conditions she never mentions - four weeks run and three readings booked. She never names the mileage record, the order of the writes or any figure gold produces, and she does not correct a wrong number. Her arc closes exactly where evaluation_criteria closes: she rings off once she has heard that the miles are on the rental and the payment went through, and asks for nothing beyond that.

REACHABILITY IN A REAL CONVERSATION. Turn by turn: she states her mobile and name, so the profile lookup has a locator; she gives two more details, so the identity check passes at its threshold of two; the booking lookup gives the reservation and its dates; the usage lookup gives the grants and readings; the charges lookup gives the overage test; the two protection lookups give the election and its fees; the agent computes 3600 and books the grant; the agent computes 814.40, tells her, and she agrees; the agent unlocks the payment and hands it to her; she runs it and the receipt comes back into the conversation. Every question a real agent would ask has an answer in the persona — what she wants, when the trip ends, how she collected the car, whether she agrees to the price — and the one thing she cannot answer, internal reference numbers, is written as a refusal with the obvious consequence that the agent uses its own lookups. Nothing waits on the host, on a workshop, on a bank or on a future date; both writes land under the one frozen clock.

WHAT A CARELESS AGENT GETS WRONG. Taking the 1500 unused miles from the reservation instead of reconciling the record (2700 miles, then a different price). Measuring the rest of the trip from today rather than from the latest reading (2700). Using the standard 125-mile daily measure (2700). Selling in 500-mile blocks (3500). Missing the lifted ceiling (1250). Missing the reserve (2700). Counting the weekend trip's overage line against this reservation (2250). On the pricing side: missing the corporate block price, or reaching it from one protection fee row instead of both (958.40), missing the volume concession (872.00), charging by the block begun rather than by the mile (908.00), assuming telematics handling (808.40), missing the early-purchase credit (854.40), or, worst, pricing before the grant is booked (0.00). A careful agent excludes each of these from the rule text and the records alone: the rule states each ladder in full, and the records show which tier the reservation sits on.

STANDARD SOLUTION. Find the member from her mobile and name; verify her on two details; read the reservations and take the live one; read its mileage record and total the grants and readings; read its charge lines and confirm no mileage overage stands on it; read the protection election on the trip and total the 1984.00 and 704.00 daily protection fees charged on it. Then compute the grant: unused 950 from the record, 24 covered days from the latest reading to the scheduled return inclusive, a 150-mile daily measure from the 63.6-mile average, a 400-mile reserve, giving 3050 miles to cover; four 900-mile blocks, 3600 miles, inside the 4250 miles of room left under the 8000-mile ceiling a long reservation with no overage carries. Book it. Then compute the price: a 125.00 block price on the corporate election, whose 2688.00 of daily protection fees clears the two-thousand-dollar corporate threshold, 8.00 concession, 117.00 net, metered by the mile over the 500-mile priced block for 842.40, plus 12.00 handling on the host-reported reading, less the 40.00 early-purchase credit, giving 814.40. Unlock the payment, hand it to her, and she pays.

VERIFICATION ACTUALLY RUN. The handling-time recomputation was run from the policies on disk with the gates' own evaluator (build_env / eval_compute / substitute from skills/erl-task-instantiate/scripts/check_compute.py) over this initial_state, with the grant write simulated before the pricing computation. Output: "B grant result= 3600" with factor baselines 2700, 2700, 2700, 3500, 1250, 2700 and an all-baseline fall-back of 1250; "A price result= 814.4" with factor baselines 958.4, 872.0, 908.0, 808.4, 854.4 and an all-baseline fall-back of 1166.0; and "A price WITHOUT B result= 0.0", the prerequisite-sensitivity run for the single edge. Every figure equals the declared expected, baseline_result and factor_sensitivity entries in computations, and the gold arguments at steps 8 and 10. The four near-misses were recomputed the same way, one substitution at a time: folding the weekend trip's overage line onto this reservation gives 2250 miles instead of 3600; totalling only one of the two protection fee rows gives 958.40 instead of 814.40; and the fuel reading, which books no miles and is filtered out by event type, leaves both figures untouched, which is why it is not claimed as a near-miss.

RULE AGAINST COMPUTE, BOTH WAYS. Forward: every binding that reads the world or makes a choice carries a verbatim quotation in compute_basis — the four aggregates over the reservation's own record (ledger_unused, reading_count, latest_reading_date, granted_to_date, overage_count, driven_miles, avg_miles_per_day), the three cross-category reads (elec_level, elec_status, elec_fees), each ladder binding, the shortfall, the blocks, the room under the ceiling and the final rounding. Backward: every load-bearing sentence of both rules is claimed by a binding. The granting rule's sentences about the standard block, the miles to cover, the standard measures, the blocks and the ceiling are claimed by block_size, shortfall, miles_unused/days_covered/reserve_miles, blocks and headroom/result; its six ladder paragraphs are claimed by miles_unused, days_covered, daily_allowance, block_size, mile_ceiling and reserve_miles. The pricing rule's sentences about what the price is worked out from, the standard line price, the standard values and the five ladders are claimed by granted_miles, line_price, net_block_price/handling_charge/early_credit and the five ladder bindings. Semantic choices are pinned in prose rather than left to the reader: the order of operations ("the line price for the miles the top-up added, with the handling charge added and the early-purchase credit taken off"), the acting base of the concession ("off each priced block", not off the line), the moment of the floor ("taken as nothing where that comes out below nothing"), the moment of rounding ("rounded to the nearest cent once at the end"), and the endpoint conventions of every day count ("with the day of return counted" / "with the day of return left out").

SOLVABILITY EVIDENCE AGAINST GOLD. Both gold writes carry their exact base lineage (one policy for the grant, two for the priced line), each eligibility quotes its base condition verbatim and cites the reservation row and field that satisfies it before the write, and each correlation key binds to the booking_id argument the tool actually receives. The stage provenance of the grant is performed_by_this_tool — nothing outside the call has to happen for miles to be added — and of the payment is established_by_prior_tool, citing step 8, which is the only honest reading: the miles it pays for exist because the preceding write put them there. No status registration stands in for an external event anywhere in this task.

DRAFT RECOMPUTATION FROM THE VISIBLE CONTEXT. With the extended yaml, the computations and gold masked, and working only from what a rollout sees — the prose of the two policies as they will be published, the two tool schemas, what the lookups return on this world, and what the persona actually says — the same two numbers come out: 3600 miles and 814.40 dollars, in that order, on that reservation, with the payment handed to the customer. The only place a second reading could arise would be the unused-mile figure, and the rule settles it outright by naming when the record is used and when the figure standing on the reservation is; and the order of the two writes, which the pricing rule's prerequisite sentence settles outright.

OVERRIDE DECLARATIONS, CLAUSE BY CLAUSE. Three base clauses are superseded by this task's policies, each named in an overwrite entry that quotes the base words and the extended words that take their place. trips_evt_mileage_allowance: "A guest may buy further miles in whole packages only" (the quantum of a purchase); "a package bought mid-trip is granted in full and charged in full even where fewer miles are eventually driven" (how many miles a mid-trip purchase adds); "capped at the plan's per-booking ceiling however long the reservation runs" (the ceiling a reservation's included miles are held to). The same package sentence is also named by the pricing policy, whose overwrite replaces it with the standard line price, because the price of a block is the other half of what that base sentence fixes. Nothing else of any base policy is departed from: every eligibility gate, the locked-rate basis, the separable-line rule and the reading-authority rule are inherited as written, and the figures this task does not touch - the plan's daily allowance at booking, the plan's overage rate, the deposit and its waiver score - are still base's.

REVISIONS. (1) Round 1. The block for long reservations was first written as one thousand miles; symptom: the granted figure fell on an exact multiple of the priced block, so two tiers of the pricing policy's line-price ladder produced the same number and the method factor could not bite. Root cause: the granting block and the priced block shared a divisor. Change: the long-reservation block became nine hundred miles, making the grant 3600 and the three line-price methods 842.40, 819.00 and 936.00. Re-run: every pricing factor moves the result. Propagated to the rule prose, the ladder, the params and both traces. (2) Round 1. The guest's driver score was first 86, which would have waived the Monthly plan's deposit and contradicted the seeded deposit line; changed to 82, below that plan's waiver score of 85, and the seed_consistency entry for the deposit line records the check. (8) Round 5, after the source audit's revision 4. The one red was F-07, and it is the same class as round 4's B-1 with its sign reversed: change_count counts every row of the extension request register, and the prose said only 'where one extension request already stands on the reservation' - a positive-sounding phrase that names no status, next to two sibling counts whose status filters the prose does name, and against base's inherited clause that a declined or expired request leaves the reservation untouched. A reader could therefore count nothing and charge nothing. Route taken: the prose moves, not the compute, because the compute's reading is the one the charge was re-scoped to in round 3 - it answers to the burden of a fresh request landing on a register that already holds others, and lodging a request is expressly not something that touches the reservation. So the count is now taken over the extension request register rather than over the reservation, and the rule says in terms that a request stands on the register whatever has become of it, naming all six states the register can hold. No overwrite is declared and none is owed: base's clause is about what a declined or expired request does to the reservation, which this rule agrees with and now cites as the very reason the count is taken over the register instead. No compute expression was touched and no scored value moved. The sweep was then re-run with the negative case added - for every aggregate, which filter it does NOT impose that a reader could assume, taken from the union of filters its siblings impose on the same table plus that table's own status and kind dimensions. Nineteen bindings carry at least one such dimension. Those now pinned in prose: what counts as an odometer reading (a fuel or battery reading is not one, whatever odometer figure it notes - which closes O-13) and that every reading counts whoever took it, since a reading another supersedes books no miles and so adds nothing, which states base's telematics and post-trip-audit rules where this sum meets them; that miles granted count whatever they were granted for; that a line once raised for a mileage overage, and a deposit line, count however they were afterwards treated; that the amount the surcharge is charged over is the base-rate lines as raised, a credit or reversal against one being a line of its own and not taken off it; that every young-driver surcharge line standing is taken together; and that the daily protection fees count however many lines they stand as and whenever they were raised. Adjudicated as not assumable and left unstated, with the reasoning recorded: billing_period and payment_channel on the charge ledger, and coverage_segment and adjustment_reason on the other product's ledger - none of these identifies the line the rule names, and the kind restriction that does is already stated. Nothing further. O-14 is answered in two parts. The half that base settles - two readings covering one handover - is no longer an invariant but a sentence of the rule, since a superseded reading books no miles. The half that remains is the LATEST tie: two mileage readings sharing a usage_date, which cannot be broken in business words because the evaluator breaks it by row order. No gate inside this difficulty's write domain can enforce it, so it is now checked mechanically by the authoring sweeper on every run, which reports 'world invariants hold: no LATEST tie, no two readings on one handover' for both tasks of this difficulty, and the check is re-run whenever either world changes. (7) Round 4, after the render-layer audit. Symptom: the published documents entailed a different number on task 1 because two things the compute fixes were never in the prose - the restriction of the fee limb to the election's daily protection fee lines (B-1 / P-1) and the single rounding of the young-driver share (B-4 / P-5) - and the renderer, having no words for them, closed both boundaries the other way. Root cause on this side: rule/compute non-equivalence of the same class as round 2's F-05, invisible from the source layer because the expression makes the intent obvious once it is in view. Change here: the fee limb now reads 'the daily protection fees charged on it' in every sentence, every ladder tier and every quotation of the pricing policy, and the sentence that states the tiers now names what is excluded - a young-driver protection surcharge, a level-change difference, an additional-driver fee, a deductible or a credit. A sweep of every binding of all four policies against its prose then pinned the rest of the class on this task's two policies: the counting conventions behind 'how long the trip has run', 'how many days of the reserved period are still to run', 'how many days have passed since a reading' and the length of the reserved period; the endpoints of the covered-period anchor's first two tiers, which now say 'both that day and the day of return counted'; which miles the purchase is priced on (those granted as a purchased top-up, not the allowance granted at confirmation); the floor on the block price less the concession; and the rounding of the line price, which the prose had put 'once at the end' while the compute rounded the line price too - the root of the render finding B-2. No compute expression was touched and no scored value moved: 3600 miles and 814.40 dollars, every factor figure and every baseline unchanged. One reading is left to a seed invariant rather than to prose: where two odometer readings share a day the latest of them is not determinable in business words, so no world of this difficulty may carry two readings on one day - as none does. (6) Round 3. A mechanical stale-figure sweep was written and run over both task files - every number in design_rationale, every factor_trace and argument_uniqueness_tracing entry, every prerequisite_closure and solvability_contract assertion - checking each against the set of figures the world, the charter and every replay variant make true, including the near-miss substitutions the dossiers themselves claim. It found one stale figure here: the change-log entry (1) reported the three line-price methods as 842.40, 770.00 and 936.00, where 770.00 was computed with the fifteen-dollar bulk concession that applied before the block became nine hundred miles; recomputed on the world that entry names, the whole-blocks-only method gives 819.00, and the entry now says so. Four figures remain outside the machine-checkable set and are adjudicated by hand: 819.00 itself and the other two line-price methods are counterfactual method figures the taken branch never evaluates, each recomputed directly; and 7.64 is the pre-change figure the round-2 symptom names, true of the moment it reports. No other assertion in this file is false of the world it names. (3) Round 2, after the source-layer audit. Symptom: the source audit found this task had a second defensible answer on both scored parameters, because the extended included-mile ceiling contradicted base's "capped at the plan's per-booking ceiling however long the reservation runs" while the policy declared only the package override, and because the block price departed from the plan's published package price with nothing declared at all (findings F-01, F-02 / 0-A, 0-B). Root cause: an override of base that was real but undeclared, in two places. Change: the ceiling clause and the package sentence are now named and replaced in the granting policy's overwrite, the pricing policy names trips_evt_mileage_allowance in its lineage and declares the package sentence superseded by its own line price, and the standard ceiling was lifted from 3750 to 5000 with the charged-reservation tier from 4500 to 6000, so that the computation document's own default grants 1250 miles rather than reading as a refusal (observation O-01). Re-run: granted_miles and purchase_amount are unchanged at 3600 and 814.40, the ceiling factor's baseline moves from 0 to 1250 and the whole-baseline fall-back with it, and every other factor figure is unchanged. (4) Round 2, the cross-difficulty evidence (finding F-06 / 0-C). Symptom: the seeded protection fee rows charged 7.64 a day on a level whose charter daily flat is 64.00, so the factor's evidence was a figure the other product could not have produced. Change: the two rows now carry 1984.00 for thirty-one days and 704.00 for eleven at the charter's 64.00 a day, the election's coverage_days and balance follow them, and the corporate threshold rose from 200.00 to 2000.00 so that the tier is reached only by totalling both rows - which also gives the pricing computation the tier-flipping near-miss it previously lacked. user_scenario:
Renata Castellano is a freelance location scout who has had the same little crossover on a long Keyturn rental since the start of August, while her own car sits in a body shop, and she is calling from a diner car park outside Ellensburg with the engine still warm. What she wants is simple and she says it early: the included miles on this rental are nearly gone, she has another three weeks of driving ahead of her, and she would rather buy more miles now than be hit with a per-mile bill at the end of the trip. She asks the desk to sort out a top-up on the rental and put it on the card the trip is already running on; she is happy for the agent to work out what it comes to, and she will do whatever has to be done at her end to pay for it.

She gives her name as Renata Castellano and her mobile as 2065512238 straight away, because that is how she always starts a call. If the agent needs more than that to be sure of her, she offers her date of birth, 1987-04-11, and then the ZIP on her billing address, 98109; pressed further she reads out her licence number, 51427360, and her email, renata.castellano@fastmail.com. She does not know any internal reference numbers and says so plainly if she is asked for one.

Asked about the trip, she can say that it started on the fifth of August and runs through to the ninth of October, that she collected the car from the host in person, and that the host photographed the odometer a couple of days ago at a coffee stop. She half remembers the app telling her she still had about 1500 included miles, but she says herself that the figure has not moved in a while and cannot be right after the driving she has done, so she asks for it to be checked. She does not know what extra miles cost, does not know how the marketplace decides how many miles to add, and will not guess at either.

When the agent tells her what the top-up comes to, she takes it without haggling and says to go ahead. Once the agent has set the payment up and handed it over to her, she completes it herself there and then, and reads the confirmation back if she is asked to. She rings off only when she has heard both that the miles are on the rental and that the payment went through; until then she stays on the line and answers what she is asked. If the agent goes quiet or sounds unsure, she says nothing more useful than that she is not in a hurry.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Pull up the member profile of the guest on the line from the mobile number and name she gives, so that the reservation behind the call can be reached at all.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Nothing about the trip can be read without the member reference number this returns; it is the locator every later lookup and both writes hang on.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Record that the caller is the member whose reservation is about to be changed, checking the date of birth and billing ZIP she states against the profile.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Money moves on this call and miles are added to a live reservation; neither may be done before the in-session identity check has passed.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read every reservation this guest holds, and on the live one the rate plan, the state, the reserved and scheduled dates, the start date, the included miles granted, the unused-mile figure standing on it and the locked daily rate.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The reserved period, the scheduled return and the actual start date are the date spans the top-up measure, the days still to run and the block tier all rest on; the unused-mile figure standing on the reservation is what the fall-back reading of the allowance would use.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the reservation's whole mileage and fuel record: the allowance granted at confirmation, every odometer reading booked against it with its date and its source, and the fuel reading taken at collection.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The included miles granted, the miles the readings have booked, how many readings there are, when the latest one was taken and where it came from decide the unused-mile basis, the covered period, the daily mile measure, the block, the reserve and the handling charge.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the priced lines standing on the guest's reservations, and in particular whether any mileage overage has been charged on the live one.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The included-mile ceiling tier turns on whether a mileage overage has been charged on this reservation, and the overage line sitting on the earlier weekend trip must be seen to be excluded.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the protection election attached to the live reservation: which level it is written at and whether it still stands.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The block price tier is decided from the protection level on this trip and from whether that election stands or is voided.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the protection lines raised on that election, with the basis and amount of each.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The corporate block price applies only where the daily protection fees charged on the trip's election reach the corporate threshold, and only the daily protection fee lines count toward it, so those lines have to be told apart and totalled.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Unlock the action that books a bought top-up of included miles against a reservation.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The first half of the unlock/call pair; it has no effect on the records and happens once for this tool.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Book the top-up of included miles onto the live reservation, adding the miles the marketplace's measure of the rest of the trip calls for.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.booking_id: The value is the row id of the guest's live reservation. Basis: the trip booking lookup returns exactly one reservation of hers in the in_progress state, priced under the 'Keyturn Monthly Rate Plan', started 2026-08-05 and scheduled to return 2026-10-09; the tool's own contract says the reference number is 'read from the trip booking lookup before the call'. Uniqueness: her other reservation is settled, ended in May and cannot take a mileage grant at all, so only one row answers the request for more miles on the rental she is driving now.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.customer_id: The value is the member reference number returned by the member profile lookup for the caller. Basis: the tool's contract says it is 'the member reference number of the guest holding that reservation, read from the member profile lookup before the call', and the reservation's own record carries that same member as the guest. Uniqueness: exactly one profile matches the mobile number and name she states, and the reservation names that member, so no other value is reachable.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.granted_miles: 3600 whole miles. The miles the top-up must cover are the daily included-mile measure times the days still to run, less the miles still unused, plus the top-up reserve. The trip started 2026-08-05 and has run 44 days at the handling date, and three odometer readings stand against it, so the unused miles are worked out from the mileage record and not from the figure standing on the reservation: 3750 granted less 1150, 1100 and 550 booked by the readings leaves 950 (the reservation's own unused-mile figure still reads 1500 and is stale). More than fourteen days of the reserved period are still to run and the latest reading was taken 2026-09-16, within the last seven days, so the days still to run run from that reading to the scheduled return of 2026-10-09 with the return day counted: 24 days. The readings have booked 2800 miles over 44 days, an average of 63.6 a day, which is more than fifty-five but not more than eighty-five, so the daily included-mile measure is 150. The reserved period runs 66 days, which is sixty or more, and the readings have booked 2800 miles, three thousand or fewer, so the top-up reserve is 400. The miles to cover are therefore 24 x 150 - 950 + 400 = 3050. The reserved period is sixty days or more and 3750 included miles have already been granted, so the block is 900 miles; the smallest whole number of blocks covering 3050 is 4, giving 3600 miles. The reserved period is sixty days or more and no mileage overage has been charged on this reservation, so the ceiling is 8000 and the room left under it is 8000 - 3750 = 4250, which does not hold 3600 down. Any agent reading the same records reaches 3600.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Set the mileage purchase up for the guest and hand it to her, since paying for miles on her own reservation is her own act.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The second write of this call is the customer's own; the agent can only unlock it and pass it over.

evaluation_criteria.objective: The guest pays for the miles now standing on her reservation, which posts the mileage purchase as its own priced line and raises the balance on the trip.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: This is the write the top-up pricing policy computes, and the terminal state the caller asked for: the miles on the rental and the purchase on her card.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.booking_id: The value is the row id of the same live reservation the miles were added to. Basis: the tool's contract says it is the reference number of the reservation 'as the desk read it out from the trip booking lookup', and the mileage purchase is priced from the miles standing on that reservation's own record. Uniqueness: only one reservation of hers is live and only one carries the purchased top-up grant, so no other value can be meant.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.customer_id: The value is the member reference number of the caller, returned by the member profile lookup. Basis: the tool's contract says it is 'the member reference number of the guest making the purchase, as the desk read it out from the member profile lookup'. Uniqueness: one profile matches what she states about herself and the reservation names that member as its guest.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.purchase_amount: 814.40 USD. The price is the line price for the miles the top-up added, plus the handling charge, less the early-purchase credit, rounded once at the end. The mileage record now carries a purchased top-up of 3600 miles, booked by the preceding write. The trip's protection election is written as 'Keyturn Business Traveler Protection' and the daily protection fees charged on it come to 1984.00 + 704.00 = 2688.00, at least the corporate threshold of two thousand dollars, and it stands active, so the block price is 125.00. The top-up added 3600 miles, at least two thousand but fewer than four thousand, and the trip has run 44 days, at least four weeks, so the volume concession is 8.00 off each priced block, leaving 117.00. The reserved period runs 66 days, sixty or more, and the top-up added at least two thousand miles, so the line price is that block price apportioned over the priced block of five hundred miles by the mile: 3600 x (117.00 / 500) = 842.40. The latest odometer reading on the reservation, taken 2026-09-16, was reported by the host, and the trip has run at least four weeks, so the handling charge is 12.00. Twenty-one days of the reserved period are still to run, more than twenty, and the readings have booked 2800 miles, more than two thousand, so the early-purchase credit is 40.00. The line comes to 842.40 + 12.00 - 40.00 = 814.40. Any agent reading the same records converges on it.

edges.condition: the reservation's mileage record carries a purchased top-up grant whose miles are the miles this purchase is being priced for
edges.policy_source: The price of a mileage top-up is fixed only after the miles it adds stand on the reservation's included-mile record.

unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false: At the frozen clock the reservation's mileage record carries one grant only, the plan allowance booked at confirmation, and three odometer readings; no grant on it is marked as a purchased top-up, so the miles a purchase could be priced for come to nothing and the line price with them.
unresolved_at_frozen_time.flips_to_true_by: Booking the top-up puts a grant of 3600 miles marked as a purchased top-up on the reservation's mileage record, so the miles the purchase is priced for become 3600 and the line price 842.40.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: The tree has a single edge, so there is only one order to take: the grant is written first and the purchase priced after it. No two writes stand in parallel here, and the purchase reads the grant through the reservation's mileage record, so no other sequence produces the same terminal state.

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Replaying the call without the grant leaves the purchased top-up miles at nothing: the line price falls from 842.40 to 0.00 and the scored purchase_amount from 814.40 to 0.00, and the reservation's mileage record ends the call without the 3600-mile grant row.

prerequisite_closure.no_user_hint: The caller asks for a top-up on the rental and for it to go on the card, and nothing else. She never mentions the reservation's mileage record, never says that miles have to be booked onto the allowance before anything can be priced, and never asks whether something has to be done first; the closest she comes to the records is doubting the unused-mile figure she half remembers from the app and asking for it to be checked. The order of the two writes reaches the agent only from the policy sentence that the price of a top-up is fixed only after the miles it adds stand on the reservation's included-mile record.
prerequisite_closure.tools_do_not_block: pay_for_mileage_topup_d571ad94 takes booking_id, customer_id and purchase_amount, mints a row id from them and creates one trips_charges row; it never looks for a grant on the reservation, never reads the mileage record, raises no error and returns the same receipt whether or not the top-up was booked first. grant_mileage_topup_0373887d is the same shape: it creates one trips_usage row from its arguments and checks nothing about the reservation. Calling the purchase first would post a line of a different amount and leave the terminal records different from gold, but no tool would refuse it.
